factual_claims.claim: The company’s results were shaped by a persistent uncertain global political and economic environment, high inflation, and cautious private investment.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: STATEMENT OF THE CHAIRMAN and MANAGEMENT REPORT: 'High global turbulence continues to restrain investments... global politics has only added to the uncertainty... This has also affected Merko’s workload... in both construction services and real estate development.'

factual_claims.claim: European central banks maintained higher interest rates, and in the Baltics, recovery was uneven, marked by consumer caution in Estonia and Latvia, contrasted with greater economic activity in Lithuania.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT IN 2025 section: 'High global turbulence... ECB ended its cycle of lowering the base interest rate in June 2025... In Estonia, the GDP decline was registered... Lithuania was the only Baltic country to avoid a more sustained economic recession... consumer confidence and companies' willingness to invest continued to keep the economy on the upswing.'

factual_claims.claim: The construction market faced a decline in private investments, leading to a higher share of public sector orders, particularly in defense and infrastructure.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: CONSTRUCTION MARKET section: 'Private sector demand declined in 2024 and remained low in 2025... The change in public sector priorities has led to a significant increase in the procurement of defence-related objects... public procurements are prevalent on the market.'

factual_claims.claim: Despite initial delays in signing new contracts, the second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: STATEMENT OF THE CHAIRMAN: 'The second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement, and preparatory efforts resulted in new major contracts.'

factual_claims.claim: Notably, preparatory efforts in Lithuania resulted in the signing of major contracts at the beginning of 2026 for the construction of the Rūdninkai defence campus phases.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: STATEMENT OF THE CHAIRMAN: 'the second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement... the most extensive and thorough preparation was carried out by our Lithuanian colleagues and in the first days of the current year resulted in the signing of the largest contracts in Merko’s history for the construction of two phases of the Rūdninkai defence campus.'

factual_claims.claim: Furthermore, strategic investments in joint ventures like Connecto contributed significantly, accounting for one-quarter of the group's net profit.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: STATEMENT OF THE CHAIRMAN: 'Connecto companies have substantially expanded their operations in Latvia and Lithuania, and in 2025 this investment in the joint venture accounted for as much as one quarter of Merko’s consolidated net profit.'

factual_claims.claim: The group's secured order book increased notably to EUR 466.9 million as of December 31, 2025, up from EUR 340.6 million a year earlier, providing a stable workload for future periods.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED

factual_claims.claim: Overall, company performance during the reporting period reflected a transition following the completion of major prior-year projects and a return to more traditional sector margins amidst competitive market conditions.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: MANAGEMENT REPORT: 'In 2024, we were engaged in several large projects that had been started in earlier years, and these were completed as planned during 2025... The pace of signing new contracts was slower in 2024 and in the first half of 2025... the second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement.'

factual_claims.claim: Despite the contraction in revenue and net profit, Merko Ehitus successfully preserved its robust capitalisation, improved its equity ratio, and expanded its secured order book.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: F12-F14 show stronger equity ratio and larger order book despite lower revenue. BALANCE SHEET and KEY INDICATORS confirm robust capitalisation.

factual_claims.claim: In line with the long-term financial objective to distribute 50-70% of annual profit as dividends, the Management Board, in coordination with the Supervisory Board, has proposed a dividend of EUR 1.25 per share from net profits brought forward, totalling EUR 22.1 million for the 2025 financial year, representing a 55% dividend rate.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: PROFIT ALLOCATION PROPOSAL: Dividends proposed EUR 22,125,000 (~22.1m) which is 55% of retained earnings after profit allocation.
